name: Memory
summary: Editing one field. The sheet carries that field alone, with the keyboard up and the required caption below it; the page it belongs to stays behind the scrim.

looseEnds.title: Viewing moved from a sheet to a page
looseEnds.detail: A memory used to open as a bottom sheet over the home. It is now a pushed page with its own back and title, and the fields are rows on a card. Nothing records what happens to the scroll position of the list behind it on the way back.
looseEnds.ask: Does returning restore the list where it was, or land at the top?

looseEnds.title: Only two of the memory's fields are drawn
looseEnds.detail: The details page shows Condition and Status. The field-states section documents between two and eight fields depending on the memory type, and nothing here says how the page grows — or whether the card scrolls.
looseEnds.ask: Confirm the page is the same card for every memory type, and what it does at eight rows.

looseEnds.title: The sheet confirms with a tick, not a button
looseEnds.detail: Close and confirm are the two 44pt controls in the sheet's toolbar. There is no Save in the footer — that slot is drawn and switched off — so the only commit is the tick at the top right.
looseEnds.ask: Is the tick the commit, and does closing discard silently?
